output_json.patch_notes:
Root cause: `StaticHandlerImpl.handle()` computed the served path as `Utils.removeDots(Utils.urlDecode(context.normalisedPath(), false))`. `removeDots`/`normalizePath` in `Utils.java` only recognize `/` as a path separator when collapsing `.`/`..` segments. On Windows, the JVM/filesystem also treats `\` as a separator, so a request like `/%5c..%5cindex.html` decodes to `/\..\index.html`, which `removeDots` leaves untouched (no `/../` pattern matches), and this string is then concatenated onto `webRoot` in `getFile()` and passed straight to `FileSystem.exists/props/readDir`. On Windows this resolves outside `webRoot`, enabling arbitrary file read (this is the exact mechanism of CVE-2019-17640, confirmed against the upstream fix commit b12f7c4 in vert-x3/vertx-web).

Fix: in `StaticHandlerImpl.handle()`, after URL-decoding the normalised request path, replace all backslashes with forward slashes *before* calling `Utils.removeDots`, so all requested paths are canonicalized and dot-segment-stripped as UNIX paths regardless of the host OS's native separator conventions. This is a single change at the shared root of every downstream sink in the alert (`getFile`, `sendStatic`, `isFileExisting`, `getFileProps`, `sendDirectory`/`sendDirectoryListing`'s `dir` argument), since they all consume the one `path` value computed in `handle()` — so encoded-backslash, literal-backslash, and mixed-separator traversal variants are all blocked, not just the single highlighted trace.

Added `StaticHandlerTest#testEscapeWindows` (mirroring upstream's regression test) asserting `/%5c..%5cindex.html` resolves to the configured index page (200 OK) instead of escaping the web root.
output_json.risk_notes: Change is scoped to a single decode/normalize step in `StaticHandlerImpl.handle()`; behavior for well-formed UNIX-style paths (the vast majority of real traffic) is unchanged since `.replace('\\','/')` is a no-op when no backslash is present. Ran the full `StaticHandlerTest` suite (57 tests) in the project's Docker container: all pass except `testHttp2Push`/`testNoHttp2Push`, which fail with `VertxException: ALPN not available for JDK SSL/TLS engine` — a pre-existing JDK/container TLS-provider limitation unrelated to this change (no path/file-handling involved). Did not modify `Utils.java` itself, since the shared-root fix in `StaticHandlerImpl` fully blocks the traversal without touching the more general-purpose normalization utilities used elsewhere in the router.
output_json.summary: Fixed CWE-022 path traversal in StaticHandlerImpl (CVE-2019-17640 class bug): on Windows, the backslash character is a path separator, but StaticHandlerImpl only decoded/normalized forward-slash dot-segments, so a URL-encoded backslash (e.g. `%5c..%5cindex.html`) survived `Utils.removeDots` unchanged and, once concatenated onto `webRoot` and handed to the filesystem, was interpreted by Windows as a `..` traversal outside the configured web root.
